messages:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — the Maris-12B model pack we pulled has two clauses that matter for us: 'non-commercial use only' and 'no redistribution of derivative weights'. Legal asked whether producing a 4-bit quantized checkpoint counts as a derivative. Also: is serving a quantized version via our Hosted API OK?

olivia: Short answer: quantized weights are almost always treated as a derivative by licensors. Need to check the exact license text + any vendor side addenda. We should not assume hosting is allowed if the license says 'non-commercial' only.

olivia: Actionable: I'll need the exact license file (PDF or repo link). If the licensor permits "inference-only" hosting, they normally require: an attribution string, no downloads, and a prohibition on redistribution of any converted weights.

olivia: Recommended attribution to show on UI/logs/metadata (example): `Model: Maris-12B — For non-commercial research use only. Copyright AcmeAI 2024. No derivative weights may be redistributed.`

maria: Ran an initial quantization pass (PTQ, 4-bit integer, per-channel). Quick eval on our instruction-following set (500 prompts):
```
FP16 baseline: helpfulness=78.2
4-bit PTQ: helpfulness=72.9 (notable drop on multi-step reasoning)
4-bit QAT (2k steps): helpfulness=76.8
```
maria: TL;DR — PTQ is cheaper but shows a measurable quality regression; QAT mostly recovers but costs 2k fine-tune steps.

lee: From infra side, hosting-only is feasible with controls: disable model download, disable embedding storage, set short logs retention, and mark model as "license_restricted" in the catalog so Dedicated/Private deploys are disallowed by default. We can add a policy gate in the console to prevent customers from exporting weights.

aj: Important product note — several Dedicated customers will expect pinned versions and on-prem options. If the license forbids redistribution, we must proactively flag this model as "no-dedicated/no-private" until we get written permission. That may affect sales conversations.

derek: A couple of technical mitigations we could consider while we get legal confirmation: server-side watermarking of responses, disable KV cache sharing across tenants, and detect commercial intent in prompts and return an error if detected. Not perfect but reduces risk surface.

olivia: Don't rely on heuristic detection for legal compliance. Those mitigations are helpful but not a substitute for permission. Next steps from Legal: (1) get the exact license text, (2) ask licensor for explicit written permission to (a) serve quantized weights via hosted API and (b) allow QAT or other transforms, (3) if allowed, get attribution text and any other boilerplate they require.

compliance-bot: New ticket created: LIC-482 (Maris-12B vendor permission request).

maria: Plan from eng-ml: put onboarding on hold, run a short QAT experiment (2k steps) to see if we can fully recover baseline, and attach eval artifacts to LIC-482. Also will include a diff of failure cases (PTQ vs QAT vs FP16).

lee: I'll add a catalog flag and a console banner for the model that displays the attribution string Olivia posted, and set default routing to block Dedicated/Private until ticket is closed.

olivia: Thanks — once we have vendor response, Legal will advise the exact hosting config. If they deny hosting, we should consider: (a) decline to onboard, or (b) host an API-only read-only wrapper under a research partnership with strict access controls and signed user agreements.

sanjay: Sounds good. I'll attach the license PDF here and ping the vendor contact. Thanks all — holding rollout until LIC-482 updates.
